# Introduction {#sec-intro}

Liquidity stress testing follows the supervisory framework [@bcbs2013]. The
classic account of bank runs is @diamond1983. Text can carry *emphasis*,
**strong emphasis** and `inline code`, and a footnote.[^horizon]

[^horizon]: The survival horizon is 30 calendar days, costing $1.2m a year to monitor.

## Scope

The framework covers three things:

- retail and wholesale deposits;
- committed credit and liquidity facilities;
- collateral calls on derivatives.

It is applied in two steps:

1. Project contractual and behavioural cash flows.
2. Compare cumulative net outflows with the liquidity buffer.

### Scenario design

Scenarios combine market-wide and firm-specific shocks.

#### Idiosyncratic stress

A two-notch downgrade triggers wholesale funding run-off of 40%.

#### Market stress

Haircuts on level 2 assets widen by 15 percentage points.

::: {.keyfinding}
The 30-day survival horizon is met in every scenario, with a minimum buffer
of 112% of net outflows.
:::

::: {.recommendation title="Next step"}
Recalibrate deposit outflow rates every quarter.
:::

# Results {#sec-results}

@fig-survival shows the survival curve and @tbl-outflows lists the outflow
assumptions discussed in @sec-intro.

|:--------------------|-------------:|-------------:|
| Stable retail       |           5% |       12,400 |
| Less stable retail  |          10% |        6,150 |
| Operational         |          25% |        3,980 |
| Non-operational     |          40% |        2,275 |

: Outflow assumptions by deposit category {#tbl-outflows}

The liquidity coverage ratio is $\mathit{LCR} = \mathit{HQLA} / \mathit{NCO} \ge 100\%$.
